abstract_sentences.text: RL training of multi-turn LLM agents is inherently unstable, and reasoning quality directly determines task performance.
Entropy is widely used to track reasoning stability.
However, entropy only measures diversity within the same input, and cannot tell whether reasoning actually responds to different inputs.
In RAGEN-2, we find that even with stable entropy, models can rely on fixed templates that look diverse but are input-agnostic.
We call this template collapse, a failure mode invisible to entropy and all existing metrics.

To diagnose this failure, we decompose reasoning quality into within-input diversity (Entropy) and cross-input distinguishability (Mutual Information, MI), and introduce a family of mutual information proxies for online diagnosis.
Across diverse tasks, mutual information correlates with final performance much more strongly than entropy, making it a more reliable proxy for reasoning quality.
We further explain template collapse with a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) mechanism.
Low reward variance weakens task gradients, letting regularization terms dominate and erase cross-input reasoning differences.
To address this, we propose SNR-Aware Filtering to select high-signal prompts per iteration using reward variance as a lightweight proxy.
Across planning, math reasoning, web navigation, and code execution, the method consistently improves both input dependence and task performance.

final_judgment.single_storyline: Stable entropy can conceal input-agnostic reasoning. MI makes that failure observable; low reward variance is proposed as the SNR condition; RV filtering is the intervention.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: It keeps the failure definition, MI proxy, SNR schematic, selection rule, main tables/figures, boundary condition, and five limitations.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: It moves environment and hyperparameter detail, alternative filtering/proxy analyses, all proofs, filtered-objective bias, and GRPO extension to p.26–44.
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 1 defines the two-dimensional blind spot; Figure 3, Table 6, and Figure 9 reuse RV to connect mechanism, intervention, and boundary.
final_judgment.largest_gap: Peak/delta aggregation and absent seed-level uncertainty make the stability of performance claims difficult to estimate; theoretical assumptions and bias caveat are appendix-dependent.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For a claimed metric blind spot, define the missing axis visually, then make diagnostic, mechanism, intervention, and failure boundary share a measurable intermediate variable.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: Use the rule when the intermediate variable has observable reliability conditions and a feasible controlled intervention; report failures when noise, bias, or confounding changes its meaning.
